chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Sama'a narrated from Muhammad ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Attar, from Hisham, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a slave who freed a sa'iba (a slave freed on condition that he remains in the master's service or his heirs inherit him). He said: 'He is under the guardianship of whomever he chooses, and upon whomever he is attached falls his liability, and he has his inheritance.' I said: 'And if he remains silent until he dies?' He said: 'His inheritance is placed in the treasury of the Muslims.'

key_terms.سَائِبَةً: Sa'iba (a slave freed with the condition that he remains under the master's care or his heirs inherit him)
key_terms.يُوَالِي: He is under the guardianship of

ai.seo_question: What are the inheritance rules for a sa'iba (freed slave) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of a *sa'iba* (a freed slave who retains no other patron) by establishing that the master of the freed slave becomes the default guardian (*wali*) and heir, assuming the associated liabilities. This ruling highlights the transition from tribal patronage to a structured inheritance system where, in the absence of a designated heir, the estate reverts to the *bayt al-mal* (public treasury), reflecting the Imamate's role in managing communal assets.
